title: fix(update): restore Gateway readiness before optional Doctor inspections
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary Gateway downtime when updates run optional Doctor inspections while the service is stopped.

## User Impact

Updates driven by this version run 12 inspection-only checks after the Gateway is ready, preserving their findings in the update result. Repairs, migrations, readiness gates, and diagnostics that cannot be reproduced by the deferred path remain in the stopped window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed updater advertises that it will finish the inspection pass after restart. Doctor defers only lint-backed, read-only checks. The finalizer runs those checks with explicit selectors and informational findings enabled, after verified readiness. An incomplete pass is advisory; uncertain child-process cleanup still propagates through the existing recovery boundary.

The capability is internal, not a new configuration option. Older installed updaters do not advertise it, so an upgrade from 2026.9.8 retains the original inspection behavior rather than losing diagnostics. `--no-restart`, unowned/stopped plugin-only services, and copied-state rehearsals retain their existing behavior. The performance improvement applies once the new updater is installed.

`session-snapshots` stays in-window because lint omits snapshot metadata scan-error diagnostics. `workspace-status` stays because lint omits errored plugin identities.

## Evidence

- Retained negative control: the deferral regression fails against the original base.
- Native before/after updates ran back-to-back in a serialized measurement lane. Every observed outage was summed. These are **single loaded-host observations, not a speedup claim**:

  | Observation | Total downtime | Stopped-window Doctor | Post-plugin lint | Deferred post-ready pass |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | Baseline | 342.872 s | 60.463 s | 12.829 s | absent |
  | Candidate | 264.819 s | 40.368 s | 12.931 s | 23.676 s |
  | Released 2026.9.8 driver → candidate | 341.960 s | 62.170 s | 12.593 s | absent, as intended for an older driver |

  Historical baseline was 537.722 s total downtime across both outages (10.452 + 527.269 s), Doctor 93.669 s, post-plugin lint 26.395 s; it is not paired performance evidence.
- **Placement proof:** the baseline trace records all 12 selected contributions during the outage (09:39:27–09:39:34 UTC, readiness restored 09:41:39). The candidate trace records none of those contributions in the stopped-window Doctor and explicitly lists all 12 as deferred. Readiness returned at 10:13:23 UTC; the Gateway verifier completed at 10:13:38, before the ledger's completed `post-activation doctor inspections` step. That result contains all 12 explicit `--only` selectors and retains the informational `core/doctor/command-owner` finding. The lint process exited 1 for that finding while the update still exited 0 with status `ok`.
- **Exact native targets:** baseline `430f975aacee445525c4663aa88ed1590f2f08b1`; installed candidate `2837aa62f4dc76d924af7b8069cbb823bd237c26` → distinct target `dc5fd696d73622e1bc1d9fd2b421957b7f0ebacb` (same change plus a non-product marker). Both finish with `/readyz` 200, matching installed and built commits.
- **Released-driver boundary:** the isolated 2026.9.8 tag installation (`fc23bc864e4553c2d215e479eeec47b67a0bf943`) successfully updated to `2837aa62f4dc76d924af7b8069cbb823bd237c26`, with matching built commit and `/readyz` 200. The original loopback/port settings, linked test plugin, and enabled bundled plugins remained intact. This is a native **released-tag source-driver** cell, not an npm tarball or Docker claim. Older-driver Doctor keeps these inspections in-window, so no diagnostics are silently dropped.
- Both affected test suites passed (108 tests), together with the core and CLI-update test typechecks. Exact-head review of `2837aa62f4dc76d924af7b8069cbb823bd237c26` found no actionable regressions.
- CI completed all selected checks. Two main-owned failures remain: the unchanged `session-dashboard` Canvas/MCP pin-click tests ([same failure on main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38038570610/job/114174218095)), and Kysely guard violations in unchanged `doctor-migration-preservation.ts` / `openclaw-migration-witness.ts` ([same failure on main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38038570610/job/114174218086)). Both main jobs ran at `02a2bd2114357de8e1d3162621aa3d2822cfe3ad`. No UI, Kysely, or migration files are changed here.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. Reverting restores in-window inspection ordering; this adds no persisted-state, schema, dependency, or public protocol change. Blast radius is update finalization and Doctor inspection timing, including plugin-only updates; inspection findings remain advisory and required repair/readiness work stays before activation.
